vst/verif_p1.v
Require Import VST.floyd.proofauto.
Require Import CPrograms.p1_abs.
#[export] Instance CompSpecs : compspecs. make_compspecs prog. Defined.
Definition Vprog : varspecs. mk_varspecs prog. Defined.
Definition abs_spec :=
 DECLARE _abs_val
 WITH x : Z
 PRE [tint]
   PROP (Int.min_signed < x <= Int.max_signed)
   PARAMS (Vint (Int.repr x)) SEP ()
 POST [tint]
   PROP () RETURN (Vint (Int.repr (Z.abs x))) SEP ().
Definition Gprog : funspecs := ltac:(with_library prog [abs_spec]).
Lemma body_abs : semax_body Vprog Gprog f_abs_val abs_spec.
Proof.
  start_function.
  forward_if.
  - forward. entailer!.
    + change (-x <= 2147483647). change (-2147483648 < x <= 2147483647) in H. lia.
    + rewrite Z.abs_neq by lia. entailer!.
  - forward. entailer!. rewrite Z.abs_eq by lia. reflexivity.
Qed.
Print Assumptions body_abs.

imports "AutoCorres2.AutoCorres"
begin

  shows "abs_val' x \<bullet> s \<lbrace> \<lambda>Res r _. r = abs x \<rbrace>"
  unfolding abs_val'_def
  apply runs_to_vcg
  subgoal using assms by (simp add: INT_MAX_def; linarith)
  subgoal by simp
  done
ML \<open>val _ = if null (Thm_Deps.all_oracles [@{thm abs_val_correct}]) then
  writeln "AUDIT: abs_val_correct has no oracle dependencies" else error "Oracle dependency detected"\<close>
end
end

void swap(int *a, int *b) {
    int t = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = t;
}

Require Import VST.floyd.proofauto.
Require Import CPrograms.p2_swap.
#[export] Instance CompSpecs : compspecs. make_compspecs prog. Defined.
Definition Vprog : varspecs. mk_varspecs prog. Defined.
Definition swap_separate_spec :=
 DECLARE _swap
 WITH a : val, b : val, x : int, y : int
 PRE [tptr tint, tptr tint]
   PROP () PARAMS (a;b)
   SEP (data_at Tsh tint (Vint x) a; data_at Tsh tint (Vint y) b)
 POST [tvoid]
   PROP () RETURN ()
   SEP (data_at Tsh tint (Vint y) a; data_at Tsh tint (Vint x) b).
Definition swap_alias_spec :=
 DECLARE _swap
 WITH p : val, x : int
 PRE [tptr tint, tptr tint]
   PROP () PARAMS (p;p) SEP (data_at Tsh tint (Vint x) p)
 POST [tvoid]
   PROP () RETURN () SEP (data_at Tsh tint (Vint x) p).
Definition Gprog : funspecs := ltac:(with_library prog [swap_separate_spec]).
Lemma body_swap_separate : semax_body Vprog Gprog f_swap swap_separate_spec.
Proof.
  start_function.
  forward. forward. forward. forward. entailer!.
Qed.
Lemma body_swap_alias : semax_body Vprog Gprog f_swap swap_alias_spec.
Proof.
  start_function.
  forward. forward. forward. forward. entailer!.
Qed.
Print Assumptions body_swap_separate.
Print Assumptions body_swap_alias.

autocorres/p2/P2.thy
theory P2
imports "AutoCorres2.AutoCorres"
begin
install_C_file "../../programs/p2_swap.c"
autocorres [heap_abs_syntax, ts_rules = nondet] "p2_swap.c"
context p2_swap_global_addresses begin
thm swap'_def
lemma swap_correct:
  "\<lbrakk>IS_VALID(32 word) s (ptr_coerce a); heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce a) = x;
    IS_VALID(32 word) s (ptr_coerce b); heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce b) = y\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow>
    swap' a b \<bullet> s \<lbrace> \<lambda>Res _ s. heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce a) = y \<and>
      heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce b) = x \<rbrace>"
  unfolding swap'_def
  by (runs_to_vcg; clarsimp simp: fun_upd_apply)
ML \<open>val _ = if null (Thm_Deps.all_oracles [@{thm swap_correct}]) then
  writeln "AUDIT: swap_correct has no oracle dependencies" else error "Oracle dependency detected"\<close>
end
end

Every mathematical prefix sum must fit in signed int. This rules out intermediate overflow, even if positive and negative terms later cancel.
C source · shared across provers
programs/p3_sum.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view
#include <limits.h>
int sum_array(const int *a, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < n) {
        s += a[i];
        i++;
    }
    return s;
}

vst/verif_p3.v
Require Import VST.floyd.proofauto.
Require Import CPrograms.p3_sum.
#[export] Instance CompSpecs : compspecs. make_compspecs prog. Defined.
Definition Vprog : varspecs. mk_varspecs prog. Defined.
Definition sumZ : list Z -> Z := fold_right Z.add 0.
Lemma sumZ_app : forall a b, sumZ (a++b) = sumZ a + sumZ b.
Proof. intros. induction a; simpl; lia. Qed.
Lemma prefix_step : forall xs i,
  0 <= i < Zlength xs ->
  sumZ (sublist 0 (i+1) xs) = sumZ (sublist 0 i xs) + Znth i xs.
Proof.
  intros. rewrite (sublist_split 0 i (i+1)) by lia.
  rewrite sumZ_app, (sublist_one i) by lia. simpl. lia.
Qed.
Definition sum_spec :=
 DECLARE _sum_array
 WITH a : val, xs : list Z, n : Z
 PRE [tptr tint, tint]
   PROP (0 <= n <= Int.max_signed; Zlength xs = n;
     Forall (fun x => Int.min_signed <= x <= Int.max_signed) xs;
     forall k, 0 <= k <= n ->
       Int.min_signed <= sumZ (sublist 0 k xs) <= Int.max_signed)
   PARAMS (a; Vint (Int.repr n))
   SEP (data_at Tsh (tarray tint n) (map (fun x => Vint (Int.repr x)) xs) a)
 POST [tint]
   PROP () RETURN (Vint (Int.repr (sumZ xs)))
   SEP (data_at Tsh (tarray tint n) (map (fun x => Vint (Int.repr x)) xs) a).
Definition Gprog : funspecs := ltac:(with_library prog [sum_spec]).
Lemma body_sum : semax_body Vprog Gprog f_sum_array sum_spec.
Proof.
  start_function. forward. forward.
  forward_while
    (EX i : Z,
      PROP (0 <= i <= n)
      LOCAL (temp _a a; temp _n (Vint (Int.repr n));
        temp _i (Vint (Int.repr i));
        temp _s (Vint (Int.repr (sumZ (sublist 0 i xs)))))
      SEP (data_at Tsh (tarray tint n) (map (fun x => Vint (Int.repr x)) xs) a)).
  - Exists 0. entailer!.
  - entailer!.
  - assert (Hi : 0 <= i < Zlength xs) by lia.
    assert (Hs := H2 (i+1) ltac:(lia)).
    rewrite prefix_step in Hs by lia.
    assert (Hsi := H2 i ltac:(lia)).
    assert (Hx : Int.min_signed <= Znth i xs <= Int.max_signed)
      by (apply Forall_Znth; auto; lia).
    forward. forward.
    forward.
    Exists (i+1). entailer!.
    rewrite prefix_step by lia. reflexivity.
  - forward. entailer!.
    autorewrite with sublist in *. reflexivity.
Qed.
Print Assumptions body_sum.

#include <limits.h>
int sum_array(const int *a, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < n) {
        s += a[i];
        i++;
    }
    return s;
}

[[rc::args("p @ &own<array<i32, {xs `at_type` int i32}>>", "n @ int<i32>")]]
[[rc::requires("{n = length xs}",
  "{∀ k, (k ≤ n)%nat → min_int i32 ≤ sumZ (take k xs) ≤ max_int i32}")]]
[[rc::returns("{sumZ xs} @ int<i32>")]]
[[rc::ensures("own p : array<i32, {xs `at_type` int i32}>")]]
[[rc::lemmas("prefix_step")]]
[[rc::tactics("all: try by pose proof (prefix_step xs j y H6); pose proof (H (S j) ltac:(lia)); lia.")]]
[[rc::tactics("all: try by rewrite Nat.add_1_r; symmetry; apply prefix_step.")]]
int sum_array(const int *a, int n) {
  int s = 0;
  int i = 0;
  [[rc::exists("j : nat")]]
  [[rc::inv_vars("i : j @ int<i32>", "s : {sumZ (take j xs)} @ int<i32>")]]
  [[rc::constraints("{(j ≤ n)%nat}")]]
  while (i < n) {
    s += a[i];
    i++;
  }
  return s;
}

refinedc/proofs/p3_sum/sum_extra.v
From refinedc.typing Require Import typing.
Definition sumZ : list Z -> Z := foldr Z.add 0.
Lemma sumZ_app xs ys : sumZ (xs ++ ys) = sumZ xs + sumZ ys.
Proof. induction xs; simpl; lia. Qed.
Lemma prefix_step xs i x :
  xs !! i = Some x ->
  sumZ (take (S i) xs) = sumZ (take i xs) + x.
Proof.
  revert i. induction xs; intros [|i] H; simpl in *; try discriminate.
  - inversion H. lia.
  - rewrite (IHxs i H). lia.
Qed.

programs/p3_sum.c
#include <limits.h>

/*@ logic integer prefix_sum{L}(int *a, integer n) =
      n <= 0 ? 0 : prefix_sum(a, n-1) + a[n-1];
*/
/*@ requires 0 <= n;
    requires n > 0 ==> \valid_read(a + (0 .. n-1));
    requires n > 0 ==> \initialized(a + (0 .. n-1));
    requires \forall integer k; 0 <= k <= n ==>
      INT_MIN <= prefix_sum(a,k) <= INT_MAX;
    assigns \nothing;
    ensures \result == prefix_sum(a,n);
*/
int sum_array(const int *a, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    int i = 0;
    /*@ loop invariant 0 <= i <= n;
        loop invariant s == prefix_sum(a,i);
        loop assigns i, s;
        loop variant n-i;
    */
    while (i < n) {
        /*@ assert prefix_sum(a,i+1) == s + (integer)a[i]; */
        s += a[i];
        i++;
    }
    return s;
}

    while (i < n) {
        s += a[i];
        i++;
    }
    return s;
}

thm sum_array'_def
definition array_values :: "lifted_globals \<Rightarrow> 32 signed word ptr \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "array_values s a xs = (\<forall>i<length xs.
    ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int i)::32 word ptr) \<and>
    sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int i))) = xs ! i)"
lemma sum_array_correct:
  assumes A: "array_values s a xs"
    and N: "n = int (length xs)" "n \<le> INT_MAX"
    and B: "\<forall>k\<le>length xs. INT_MIN \<le> sum_list (take k xs) \<and> sum_list (take k xs) \<le> INT_MAX"
  shows "sum_array' a n \<bullet> s \<lbrace>\<lambda>Res r s'. r = sum_list xs \<and> s' = s\<rbrace>"
proof -
  have access: "\<And>i. 0 \<le> i \<Longrightarrow> i < n \<Longrightarrow>
    ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i)::32 word ptr) \<and>
    sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i))) = xs ! nat i"
  proof -
    fix i::int assume I: "0 \<le> i" "i < n"
    have "nat i < length xs" using I N by linarith
    with A have "ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int (nat i))::32 word ptr) \<and>
      sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int (nat i)))) = xs ! nat i"
      unfolding array_values_def by blast
    then show "ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i)::32 word ptr) \<and>
      sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i))) = xs ! nat i" using I by simp
  qed
  have step: "\<And>i. 0 \<le> i \<Longrightarrow> i < n \<Longrightarrow>
    sum_list (take (nat i) xs) + sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i))) =
      sum_list (take (nat (i+1)) xs)"
  proof -
    fix i::int assume I: "0 \<le> i" "i < n"
    have "nat i < length xs" using I N by linarith
    then show "sum_list (take (nat i) xs) + sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i))) =
      sum_list (take (nat (i+1)) xs)"
      using access[OF I] I by (simp add: nat_add_distrib take_Suc_conv_app_nth)
  qed
  show ?thesis
  unfolding sum_array'_def
  supply runs_to_whileLoop_res [where
    I="\<lambda>(i,acc) s'. 0 \<le> i \<and> i \<le> n \<and> acc = sum_list (take (nat i) xs) \<and> s' = s" and
    R="measure' (\<lambda>((i,acc),s'). nat (n-i))", runs_to_vcg]
  apply runs_to_vcg
  subgoal using access by blast
  subgoal premises prems for i
  proof -
    have L: "nat (i+1) \<le> length xs" using prems N by linarith
    have "INT_MIN \<le> sum_list (take (nat (i+1)) xs)" using B L by blast
    then show ?thesis using step[of i] prems by (simp add: INT_MIN_def INT_MAX_def)
  qed
  subgoal premises prems for i
  proof -
    have L: "nat (i+1) \<le> length xs" using prems N by linarith
    have "sum_list (take (nat (i+1)) xs) \<le> INT_MAX" using B L by blast
    then show ?thesis using step[of i] prems by simp
  qed
  subgoal by linarith
  subgoal using N by linarith
  subgoal by linarith
  subgoal by linarith
  subgoal using step by blast
  subgoal using N by auto
  subgoal using N by simp
  done
qed
ML \<open>val _ = if null (Thm_Deps.all_oracles [@{thm sum_array_correct}]) then

end

✓ Checked · manual proof
A nondecreasing array may contain duplicates. A half-open interval and lo+(hi-lo)/2 avoid overflow; the postcondition covers both a valid matching index and key absence.
C source · shared across provers
programs/p4_binary_search.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view

int binary_search(const int *a, int n, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = n;
    while (lo < hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2;
        if (a[mid] == key) return mid;
        if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid+1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    return -1;
}

Require Import VST.floyd.proofauto.
Require Import CPrograms.p4_binary_search.
#[export] Instance CompSpecs : compspecs. make_compspecs prog. Defined.
Definition Vprog : varspecs. mk_varspecs prog. Defined.
Lemma div_two_repr : forall d, 0 <= d <= Int.max_signed ->
  Int.divs (Int.repr d) (Int.repr 2) = Int.repr (d/2).
Proof.
  intros. unfold Int.divs.
  rewrite !Int.signed_repr by rep_lia.
  rewrite Z.quot_div_nonneg by lia. reflexivity.
Qed.
Definition search_spec :=
 DECLARE _binary_search
 WITH a : val, xs : list Z, n : Z, key : Z
 PRE [tptr tint, tint, tint]
   PROP (0 <= n <= Int.max_signed; Zlength xs = n;
     Int.min_signed <= key <= Int.max_signed;
     Forall (fun x => Int.min_signed <= x <= Int.max_signed) xs;
     forall i j, 0 <= i /\ i <= j /\ j < n -> Znth i xs <= Znth j xs)
   PARAMS (a; Vint (Int.repr n); Vint (Int.repr key))
   SEP (data_at Tsh (tarray tint n) (map (fun x => Vint (Int.repr x)) xs) a)
 POST [tint] EX res : Z,
   PROP (-1 <= res < n;
     0 <= res -> Znth res xs = key;
     res = -1 <-> forall i, 0 <= i < n -> Znth i xs <> key)
   RETURN (Vint (Int.repr res))
   SEP (data_at Tsh (tarray tint n) (map (fun x => Vint (Int.repr x)) xs) a).
Definition Gprog : funspecs := ltac:(with_library prog [search_spec]).
Lemma body_search : semax_body Vprog Gprog f_binary_search search_spec.
Proof.
  start_function. forward. forward.
  forward_while
    (EX lo : Z, EX hi : Z,
      PROP (0 <= lo /\ lo <= hi /\ hi <= n;
        forall i, 0 <= i < lo -> Znth i xs < key;
        forall i, hi <= i < n -> key < Znth i xs)
      LOCAL (temp _a a; temp _n (Vint (Int.repr n));
        temp _key (Vint (Int.repr key));
        temp _lo (Vint (Int.repr lo)); temp _hi (Vint (Int.repr hi)))
      SEP (data_at Tsh (tarray tint n) (map (fun x => Vint (Int.repr x)) xs) a)).
  - Exists 0 n. entailer!; intros; lia.
  - entailer!.
  - assert (Hm : lo <= lo+(hi-lo)/2 < hi) by
      (pose proof (Z.div_pos (hi-lo) 2 ltac:(lia) ltac:(lia));
       pose proof (Z.div_lt_upper_bound (hi-lo) 2 (hi-lo) ltac:(lia) ltac:(lia)); lia).
    forward. { entailer!.
      rewrite div_two_repr by rep_lia.
      rewrite Int.signed_repr by rep_lia.
      split; [rep_lia | intros [_ Hb]; discriminate]. }
    rewrite sub_repr, div_two_repr, add_repr by rep_lia.
    forward. forward_if.
    + forward. Exists (lo+(hi-lo)/2). entailer!.
      assert (Hb : Int.min_signed <= Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs <= Int.max_signed)
        by (apply Forall_Znth; auto; lia).
      change (Int.repr (Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs) = Int.repr key) in H7.
      apply (f_equal Int.signed) in H7.
      rewrite !Int.signed_repr in H7 by lia.
      split; [auto | split; [lia | intro Ha; exfalso; apply (Ha (lo+(hi-lo)/2) ltac:(lia)); auto]].
    + forward. forward_if.
      * forward. { entailer!.
          change (Int.min_signed <= Int.signed (Int.repr (lo+(hi-lo)/2)) + 1 <= Int.max_signed).
          rewrite Int.signed_repr by rep_lia. rep_lia. }
        Exists (lo+(hi-lo)/2+1,hi). entailer!.
        split; [lia | split; [lia |]]. intros i Hi.
        assert (Hb : Int.min_signed <= Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs <= Int.max_signed)
          by (apply Forall_Znth; auto; lia).
        change (Int.signed (Int.repr (Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs)) < key) in H8.
        rewrite Int.signed_repr in H8 by lia.
        pose proof (H3 i (lo+(hi-lo)/2) ltac:(lia)). lia.
      * forward. Exists (lo,lo+(hi-lo)/2). entailer!.
        split; [lia | split; [lia |]]. intros i Hi.
        assert (Hb : Int.min_signed <= Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs <= Int.max_signed)
          by (apply Forall_Znth; auto; lia).
        change (Int.signed (Int.repr (Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs)) >= key) in H8.
        rewrite Int.signed_repr in H8 by lia.
        change (Int.repr (Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs) <> Int.repr key) in H7.
        assert (Hneq : Znth (lo+(hi-lo)/2) xs <> key) by congruence.
        pose proof (H3 (lo+(hi-lo)/2) i ltac:(lia)). lia.
  - forward. Exists (-1). entailer!.
    split; [|auto]. intros _ i Hi.
    destruct (Z_lt_dec i lo).
    + pose proof (H5 i ltac:(lia)). lia.
    + pose proof (H6 i ltac:(lia)). lia.
Qed.

✓ Checked · manual proof
A nondecreasing array may contain duplicates. A half-open interval and lo+(hi-lo)/2 avoid overflow; the postcondition covers both a valid matching index and key absence.
C source · shared across provers
programs/p4_binary_search.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view

int binary_search(const int *a, int n, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = n;
    while (lo < hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2;
        if (a[mid] == key) return mid;
        if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid+1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    return -1;
}

#include <refinedc.h>

[[rc::parameters("p : loc", "xs : {list Z}", "n : nat", "key : Z")]]
[[rc::args("p @ &own<array<i32, {xs `at_type` int i32}>>", "n @ int<i32>", "key @ int<i32>")]]
[[rc::requires("{n = length xs}",
  "{∀ i j x y, (i ≤ j)%nat → xs !! i = Some x → xs !! j = Some y → x ≤ y}")]]
[[rc::exists("res : Z")]]
[[rc::returns("res @ int<i32>")]]
[[rc::ensures("{(-1 ≤ res < n)%Z}",
  "{0 ≤ res → xs !! Z.to_nat res = Some key}",
  "{res = -1 ↔ ∀ i, xs !! i ≠ Some key}",
  "own p : array<i32, {xs `at_type` int i32}>")]]
[[rc::tactics("all: try by split; [intro; exfalso; solve_goal | intro Hnone; exfalso; apply (Hnone _ H14)].")]]
[[rc::tactics("all: try by have Hxy : x ≤ y := H i (Z.to_nat (vl + (vh-vl) `quot` 2)) x y ltac:(solve_goal) H25 H14; lia.")]]
[[rc::tactics("all: try by have Hyx : y ≤ x := H (Z.to_nat (vl + (vh-vl) `quot` 2)) i y x H22 H14 H23; lia.")]]
[[rc::tactics("all: try by split; [intros _ i Hi; destruct (decide (i < vl)%nat) as [Hil|Hil]; [pose proof (H2 i key Hil Hi); lia | pose proof (H3 i key ltac:(lia) Hi); lia] | done].")]]
int binary_search(const int *a, int n, int key) {
  int lo = 0;
  int hi = n;
  [[rc::exists("vl : nat", "vh : nat")]]
  [[rc::inv_vars("lo : vl @ int<i32>", "hi : vh @ int<i32>")]]
  [[rc::constraints("{(vl ≤ vh ≤ n)%nat}",
    "{∀ i x, (i < vl)%nat → xs !! i = Some x → x < key}",
    "{∀ i x, (vh ≤ i)%nat → xs !! i = Some x → key < x}")]]
  while (lo < hi) {
    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
    if (a[mid] == key) return mid;
    if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid + 1;
    else hi = mid;
  }
  return -1;
}

A nondecreasing array may contain duplicates. A half-open interval and lo+(hi-lo)/2 avoid overflow; the postcondition covers both a valid matching index and key absence.
C source · shared across provers
programs/p4_binary_search.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view

int binary_search(const int *a, int n, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = n;
    while (lo < hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2;
        if (a[mid] == key) return mid;
        if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid+1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    return -1;
}

programs/p4_binary_search.c
/*@ requires 0 <= n;
    requires n > 0 ==> \valid_read(a + (0 .. n-1));
    requires n > 0 ==> \initialized(a + (0 .. n-1));
    requires \forall integer i,j; 0 <= i <= j < n ==> a[i] <= a[j];
    assigns \nothing;
    ensures -1 <= \result < n;
    ensures \result >= 0 ==> a[\result] == key;
    ensures \result == -1 <==> (\forall integer i; 0 <= i < n ==> a[i] != key);
*/
int binary_search(const int *a, int n, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = n;
    /*@ loop invariant 0 <= lo <= hi <= n;
        loop invariant \forall integer i; 0 <= i < lo ==> a[i] < key;
        loop invariant \forall integer i; hi <= i < n ==> a[i] > key;
        loop assigns lo, hi;
        loop variant hi-lo;
    */
    while (lo < hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2;
        if (a[mid] == key) return mid;
        if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid+1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    return -1;
}

AutoCorres2
✓ Checked · manual proof
A nondecreasing array may contain duplicates. A half-open interval and lo+(hi-lo)/2 avoid overflow; the postcondition covers both a valid matching index and key absence.
C source · shared across provers
programs/p4_binary_search.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view

int binary_search(const int *a, int n, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = n;
    while (lo < hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2;
        if (a[mid] == key) return mid;
        if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid+1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    return -1;
}

theory P4
imports "AutoCorres2.AutoCorres"
begin
install_C_file "../../programs/p4_binary_search.c"
autocorres [ts_rules = nondet] "p4_binary_search.c"
context p4_binary_search_global_addresses begin
lemma mid_bounds:
  fixes lo hi :: int
  assumes "0 \<le> lo" "lo < hi"
  shows "lo \<le> lo + (hi-lo) sdiv 2 \<and> lo + (hi-lo) sdiv 2 < hi"
  using assms by (simp add: signed_divide_int_def sgn_if; presburger)
definition array_values :: "lifted_globals \<Rightarrow> 32 signed word ptr \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "array_values s a xs = (\<forall>i<length xs.
    ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int i)::32 word ptr) \<and>
    sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int i))) = xs ! i)"
lemma binary_search_correct:
  assumes A: "array_values s a xs"
    and N: "n = int (length xs)" "n \<le> INT_MAX"
    and K: "INT_MIN \<le> key" "key \<le> INT_MAX"
    and S: "\<forall>i j. i \<le> j \<and> j < length xs \<longrightarrow> xs!i \<le> xs!j"
  shows "binary_search' a n key \<bullet> s \<lbrace>\<lambda>Res r s'.
    -1 \<le> r \<and> r < n \<and> (0 \<le> r \<longrightarrow> xs ! nat r = key) \<and>
    (r = -1 \<longleftrightarrow> key \<notin> set xs) \<and> s' = s\<rbrace>"
proof -
  have access: "\<And>i. 0 \<le> i \<Longrightarrow> i < n \<Longrightarrow>
    ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i)::32 word ptr) \<and>
    sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i))) = xs ! nat i"
  proof -
    fix i::int assume I: "0 \<le> i" "i < n"
    have "nat i < length xs" using I N by linarith
    with A have "ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int (nat i))::32 word ptr) \<and>
      sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p int (nat i)))) = xs ! nat i"
      unfolding array_values_def by blast
    then show "ptr_valid (heap_typing s) (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i)::32 word ptr) \<and>
      sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p i))) = xs ! nat i" using I by simp
  qed
  show ?thesis
  unfolding binary_search'_def
  supply runs_to_whileLoop_exn' [where
    I="\<lambda>r s'. case r of Result (hi,lo) \<Rightarrow>
      (0 \<le> lo \<and> lo \<le> hi \<and> hi \<le> n \<and> s' = s \<and>
      (\<forall>i<nat lo. xs!i < key) \<and> (\<forall>i. nat hi \<le> i \<and> i < length xs \<longrightarrow> key < xs!i))
      | Exn k \<Rightarrow> (0 \<le> k \<and> k < n \<and> xs!nat k = key \<and> s' = s)" and
    R="measure' (\<lambda>((hi,lo),s'). nat (hi-lo))", runs_to_vcg]
  apply runs_to_vcg
  apply (insert N K S access)
  apply (auto simp: INT_MIN_def INT_MAX_def signed_divide_int_def sgn_if)
  subgoal premises prems for hi lo
  proof -
    let ?m = "lo + (hi-lo) div 2"
    have M: "0 \<le> ?m" "?m < n" using prems by presburger+
    have R: "sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p ?m))) = xs ! nat ?m"
      using access[OF M] by blast
    have W: "sint (word_of_int key::32 word) = key"
      using K by (simp add: sint_of_int_eq INT_MIN_def INT_MAX_def)
    show ?thesis using R W prems by auto
  qed
  subgoal premises prems for hi lo i
  proof -
    let ?m = "lo + (hi-lo) div 2"
    have MB: "lo \<le> ?m \<and> ?m < hi"
      using mid_bounds[of lo hi] prems by (simp add: signed_divide_int_def sgn_if)
    have M0: "0 \<le> ?m" using MB prems by linarith
    have M1: "nat ?m < length xs" using MB M0 prems by linarith
    have E: "nat (?m+1) = Suc (nat ?m)" using M0 by (simp add: nat_add_distrib)
    have M2: "i \<le> nat ?m" using E prems by linarith
    have "xs!i \<le> xs!nat ?m" using S M1 M2 by blast
    then show ?thesis using prems by linarith
  qed
  subgoal premises prems for hi lo i
  proof -
    let ?m = "lo + (hi-lo) div 2"
    have MB: "lo \<le> ?m \<and> ?m < hi"
      using mid_bounds[of lo hi] prems by (simp add: signed_divide_int_def sgn_if)
    have M: "0 \<le> ?m" "?m < n" using MB prems by linarith+
    have R: "sint (heap_w32 s (ptr_coerce (a +\<^sub>p ?m))) = xs ! nat ?m"
      using access[OF M] by blast
    have NE: "xs ! nat ?m \<noteq> key" using R prems by (metis of_int_sint)
    have "xs!nat ?m \<le> xs!i" using S prems by blast
    then show ?thesis using NE prems by linarith
  qed
  subgoal premises prems for hi
  proof -
    obtain i where I: "i < length xs" "xs!i = key" using prems by (auto simp: in_set_conv_nth)
    show False
    proof (cases "i < nat hi")
      case True
      have "xs!i < key" using prems True by blast
      then show False using I by simp
    next
      case False
      have "nat hi \<le> i" using False by simp
      then have "key < xs!i" using prems I by blast
      then show False using I by simp
    qed
  qed
  done
qed
ML \<open>val _ = if null (Thm_Deps.all_oracles [@{thm binary_search_correct}]) then
  writeln "AUDIT: binary_search_correct has no oracle dependencies" else error "Oracle dependency detected"\<close>
end
end

programs/p5_reverse.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view
struct node { int value; struct node *next; };
struct node *reverse(struct node *l) {
    struct node *r = 0;
    while (l != 0) {
        struct node *next = l->next;
        l->next = r;
        r = l;
        l = next;
    }
    return r;
}

Require Import VST.floyd.proofauto.
Require Import CPrograms.p5_reverse.
#[export] Instance CompSpecs : compspecs. make_compspecs prog. Defined.
Definition Vprog : varspecs. mk_varspecs prog. Defined.
Definition tnode := Tstruct _node noattr.
Fixpoint listrep (xs : list int) (p : val) : mpred :=
  match xs with
  | nil => !! (p = nullval) && emp
  | x :: tl => EX q : val, data_at Tsh tnode (Vint x,q) p * listrep tl q
  end.
Arguments listrep xs p : simpl never.
Lemma listrep_local : forall xs p,
  listrep xs p |-- !! (is_pointer_or_null p /\ (p = nullval <-> xs = nil)).
Proof.
  induction xs; intros; unfold listrep; fold listrep.
  - entailer!. tauto.
  - Intros q. entailer!.
    assert (isptr p) by auto with field_compatible.
    split; intro He; [subst p; contradiction | discriminate].
Qed.
#[export] Hint Resolve listrep_local : saturate_local.
Lemma listrep_valid : forall xs p, listrep xs p |-- valid_pointer p.
Proof.
  intros. destruct xs; unfold listrep; fold listrep.
  - entailer!.
  - Intros q. auto with valid_pointer.
Qed.
#[export] Hint Resolve listrep_valid : valid_pointer.
Definition reverse_spec :=
 DECLARE _reverse
 WITH xs : list int, p : val
 PRE [tptr tnode] PROP () PARAMS (p) SEP (listrep xs p)
 POST [tptr tnode] EX q : val,
   PROP () RETURN (q) SEP (listrep (rev xs) q).
Definition Gprog : funspecs := ltac:(with_library prog [reverse_spec]).
Lemma body_reverse : semax_body Vprog Gprog f_reverse reverse_spec.
Proof.
  start_function. forward.
  forward_while
    (EX ys : list int, EX zs : list int, EX r : val, EX l : val,
      PROP (xs = rev ys ++ zs)
      LOCAL (temp _r r; temp _l l)
      SEP (listrep ys r; listrep zs l)).
  - Exists (@nil int) xs nullval p. unfold listrep at 2. entailer!.
  - entailer!.
  - destruct zs as [|z zs].
    + unfold listrep at 2. Intros. contradiction.
    + unfold listrep at 2; fold listrep. Intros q.
      forward. forward. forward. forward.
      Exists (z::ys,zs,l,q). entailer!.
      * simpl. rewrite <- app_assoc. reflexivity.
      * unfold listrep at 3; fold listrep. Exists r. cancel.
  - assert_PROP (zs = nil) by (entailer!; tauto). subst zs.
    forward. Exists r.
    rewrite app_nil_r, rev_involutive. entailer!. unfold listrep. entailer!.
Qed.
Print Assumptions body_reverse.

struct node { int value; struct node *next; };
struct node *reverse(struct node *l) {
    struct node *r = 0;
    while (l != 0) {

#include <refinedc.h>

typedef struct [[rc::refined_by("xs : {list Z}")]]
  [[rc::typedef("node_t : {maybe2 cons xs} @ optionalO<λ (x, xs). &own<...>>")]] node {
  [[rc::field("x @ int<i32>")]]
  int value;
  [[rc::field("xs @ node_t")]]
  struct node *next;
} *node_t;

[[rc::parameters("xs : {list Z}")]]
[[rc::args("xs @ node_t")]]
[[rc::returns("{rev xs} @ node_t")]]
struct node *reverse(struct node *l) {
  struct node *r = 0;
  [[rc::exists("ys : {list Z}", "zs : {list Z}")]]
  [[rc::inv_vars("r : ys @ node_t", "l : zs @ node_t")]]
  [[rc::constraints("{xs = rev ys ++ zs}")]]
  while (l != 0) {
    struct node *next = l->next;
    l->next = r;
    r = l;
    l = next;
  }
  return r;
}

    ensures \forall integer n,i; list{Pre}(\at(l,Pre),n) && 0 <= i < n ==>

struct node *reverse(struct node *l) {

The inductive/recursive list predicates describe finite valid lists. VST and RefinedC prove reversed value sequences. AutoCorres2 also proves reversed node identities and preserves values; WP attempts that stronger contract but remains partial.
C source · shared across provers
programs/p5_reverse.c — ACSL comments omitted in this view
struct node { int value; struct node *next; };
struct node *reverse(struct node *l) {
    struct node *r = 0;
    while (l != 0) {
        struct node *next = l->next;
        l->next = r;
        r = l;
        l = next;
    }
    return r;
}

(* Adapted from AFP AutoCorres2/tests/examples/ListRev.thy.
 * Copyright 2020 Data61, CSIRO; Copyright 2022 Apple Inc.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause *)
theory P5
imports "AutoCorres2.AutoCorres"
begin
install_C_file "../../programs/p5_reverse.c"
autocorres [heap_abs_syntax] "p5_reverse.c"
context p5_reverse_global_addresses begin
primrec listrep :: "lifted_globals \<Rightarrow> node_C ptr \<Rightarrow> node_C ptr list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "listrep s p [] = (p = NULL)"
| "listrep s p (x#xs) = (p = x \<and> p \<noteq> NULL \<and>
     ptr_valid (heap_typing s) p \<and> listrep s (s[p]\<rightarrow>next) xs)"
lemma list_empty [simp]: "listrep s NULL xs = (xs = [])"
  by (induct xs) auto
lemma list_in [simp]: "\<lbrakk>listrep s p xs; p \<noteq> NULL\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> p \<in> set xs"
  by (induct xs) auto
lemma list_non_NULL:
  "p \<noteq> NULL \<Longrightarrow> listrep s p xs =
    (\<exists>ys. xs = p#ys \<and> ptr_valid (heap_typing s) p \<and> listrep s (s[p]\<rightarrow>next) ys)"
  by (cases xs) auto
lemma list_unique: "listrep s p xs \<Longrightarrow> listrep s p ys \<Longrightarrow> xs = ys"
  by (induct xs arbitrary: p ys) (auto simp: list_non_NULL)
lemma list_append_Ex: "listrep s p (xs @ ys) \<Longrightarrow> (\<exists>q. listrep s q ys)"
  by (induct xs arbitrary: p) auto
lemma list_distinct [simp]: "listrep s p xs \<Longrightarrow> distinct xs"
  apply (induct xs arbitrary: p)
   apply simp
  apply (clarsimp dest!: split_list)
  apply (frule list_append_Ex)
  apply (auto dest: list_unique)
  done
lemma list_heap_update_ignore [simp]:
  "q \<notin> set xs \<Longrightarrow> listrep (s[q\<rightarrow>next := v]) p xs = listrep s p xs"
  by (induct xs arbitrary: p) (auto simp: fun_upd_def)
definition "the_list s p = (THE xs. listrep s p xs)"
lemma the_list_val [simp]: "listrep s p xs \<Longrightarrow> the_list s p = xs"
  unfolding the_list_def by (metis list_unique the_equality)
lemma the_list_update [simp]:
  "\<lbrakk>q \<notin> set xs; listrep s p xs\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow>
     the_list s[q\<rightarrow>next := v] p = the_list s p"
  by (metis list_heap_update_ignore the_list_val)
definition "reverse_inv xs s0 l r s =
  (\<exists>ys zs. listrep s l ys \<and> listrep s r zs \<and>
    rev xs = rev ys @ zs \<and> distinct (rev xs) \<and>
    (\<forall>p \<in> set xs. s[p]\<rightarrow>value = s0[p]\<rightarrow>value))"
lemmas runs_to_whileLoop2 = runs_to_whileLoop_res' [split_tuple C and B arity: 2]
lemma reverse_correct:
  "listrep s p xs \<Longrightarrow> reverse' p \<bullet> s
    \<lbrace>\<lambda>Res r s'. listrep s' r (rev xs) \<and>
      (\<forall>p \<in> set xs. s'[p]\<rightarrow>value = s[p]\<rightarrow>value)\<rbrace>"
  unfolding reverse'_def
  apply runs_to_vcg
  apply (rule runs_to_whileLoop2 [where
    I="\<lambda>(l,r) s'. reverse_inv xs s l r s'" and
    R="measure (\<lambda>((l,r),s). length (the_list s l))",
    unfolded reverse_inv_def])
  subgoal by simp
  subgoal by simp
  subgoal by (simp split: prod.splits)
  supply distinct_rev[simp del]
  apply runs_to_vcg
  subgoal using list_non_NULL by blast
  subgoal for p_ys p_zs s1 ys zs
    apply (case_tac ys, fastforce)
    apply clarsimp
    subgoal for ys'
      apply (rule_tac x=ys' in exI)
      apply (simp add: fun_upd_def)
      done
    done
  subgoal for p_ys p_zs s1 ys zs
    apply (case_tac ys, fastforce)
    apply clarsimp
    subgoal for ys'
      apply (subgoal_tac "the_list s1 p_ys = (p_ys#ys')")
       apply (simp only:)
       apply simp
      apply simp
      done
    done
  done
ML \<open>val _ = if null (Thm_Deps.all_oracles [@{thm reverse_correct}]) then
  writeln "AUDIT: reverse_correct has no oracle dependencies" else error "Oracle dependency detected"\<close>
end
end

About this experiment


A comparative experiment · 2026-10-19


Five C programs. Four installed tools.
19/20 checks complete under the displayed contracts.


For a researcher coming from Frama-C/WP, Dafny and Rocq, with a separate lens on RL rewards for loop-invariant generation.


VST, RefinedC and AutoCorres2 check all five programs. WP checks P1–P4; its list-reversal proof stays open. Every positive result links to real proof sources and checker output in this page.


The contracts have different ownership, framing and termination guarantees. This is a small case study, not a universal ranking.


Select a program and prover in the lab. Proof replay controls move only through proof commands. Everything needed to read this page is embedded; external links are background references only.

All four tools are installed in isolated project containers. No permission change was required; the earlier installation-blocked diagnosis was incorrect.
Checked means the final function proof succeeds from its source, without admitted project goals. VST checks semax_body; RefinedC checks generated typed_function theorems; AutoCorres2 checks runs_to and rejects oracle dependencies; WP requires every generated JSON VC to pass, including RTE obligations. Exit code 0 alone is insufficient for WP.
VST and RefinedC proofs establish safety and functional partial correctness; separate termination proofs were not supplied. AutoCorres2 proves total correctness. WP also generates termination obligations. No binary/compiler-link theorem was instantiated.

# RefinedC verification framework ([webpage](https://plv.mpi-sws.org/refinedc/))

This repository contains the source code of **RefinedC**: a foundational
verification framework targeted at idiomatic C code. Thanks to its frontend
(written in OCaml), RefinedC automatically translates annotated C source code
into a deep embedding of our **Caesium** C semantics (in Coq), together with
corresponding function specs expressed using ownership and refinement types.
After this generation step, the RefinedC automation (built using our logic
programming framework called **Lithium**) takes over to prove user-defined
function specs (which can encode full functional correctness), possibly
leaving some (pure) side-conditions for the user to prove. To resolve such
side-conditions, the user can either extend the RefinedC automation or write
interactive Coq proofs. The RefinedC type system itself is also extensible to
allow expert users to add support for specific programming idioms through new
typing rules. Such additions must be proven sound against the semantic model
of RefinedC, which is encoded in [Iris](https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/iris)
(a modern framework for higher-order, concurrent separation logic).

## Documentation

The following files contain documentation about RefinedC:

- [ANNOTATIONS.md](ANNOTATIONS.md): Describes the annotation syntax
  accepted by the RefinedC frontend
- [FAQ.md](FAQ.md): Describes solutions to frequently asked questions
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): Gives an high-level overview of
  the layout of this repository.
- [DEVELOPERS.md](DEVELOPERS.md): Information for RefinedC developers.

There is a work in progress tutorial in [tutorial/](tutorial/) which
is also available in a standalone repository here:
https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/msammler/refinedc-tutorial

## Installing RefinedC

RefinedC is known to compile with Coq 9.1.0, on 64-bits Linux machines. It
also possibly works on MacOS. In any case, we strongly advise you to rely on
[opam](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html) to install dependencies.

Note that if you want to develop RefinedC or build the examples
shipped with RefinedC, you should install RefinedC according to the
instructions in [DEVELOPERS.md](DEVELOPERS.md).

### tl;dr

Assuming an appropriate [opam](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html) switch
(OCaml version 4.14.0 at least), run the following commands.
```bash
opam repo add coq-released "https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released"
opam repo add iris-dev "https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/opam.git"
opam update
opam pin add -n -y cerberus-lib "git+https://github.com/rems-project/cerberus.git#f11e6b335a687c1b77539f7e5695607d09dfc3ea"
opam pin add refinedc "git+https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/refinedc.git"
```

If the `refinedc` command it not in the `PATH` and you installed
`refinedc` in an opam switch, try `eval $(opam env)` in the directory
where you created the switch.

### System dependencies

The frontend also requires a C compiler (accessible through `cc`). A standard
GCC or Clang installation should do the trick.

### Setting up [opam](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html)

First, make sure that the OCaml package manager `opam` is installed. To do so
you can check if the following command succeeds.
```bash
opam --version
```
If you already have `opam` version 2.1.0 or higher, then you can skip to the
next section.

Otherwise, install `opam` using your usual package manager (checking that a
recent enough version is available), or run the following command (taken from
the [official installation guide](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html)).
```bash
sh <(curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ocaml/opam/master/shell/install.sh)
```
You can use the `BINDIR` environment variable to choose where the binary is
installed. There is a reasonable default but it needs root privileges.

### Setting up an [opam](https://opam.ocaml.org) switch (optional)

If you are an OCaml user and if you know what you are doing, it is perfectly
fine to install RefinedC in any "opam switch" you like (provided the OCaml
version is 4.14.0 or higher) and you can skip this section.

In the following instructions we are going to create an "opam switch" (i.e., a
fresh OCaml environment) in which RefinedC can be installed and used. Creating
a new switch is a good way to make sure that other OCaml projects are not at
all impacted, even if they have conflicting dependencies. It makes sense to
follow these steps even if you are a practiced OCamler.

The "opam swith" we are going to create will be tied to a particular directory
of your system, and the corresponding OCaml environment (including `refinedc`)
will only be accessible form a shell when working under this directory. If you
are not quite sure what to do, simply create a new directory under which all
of you RefinedC will be placed. And then create the new switch in that folder.
```bash
mkdir refinedc-projects
opam switch create refinedc-projects ocaml-variants.4.14.2+options ocaml-option-flambda
```
You should then have an appropriate OCaml environment (with version 4.14.0) in
the `refinedc-projects` directory (or whatever you named it). In the following
we will assume that everything you do will be under that directory, so do not
forget to move into it.
```bash
cd refinedc-projects
```

### Installing RefinedC and its dependencies

RefinedC requires Coq, Iris, as well as a number of OCaml dependencies. These
dependencies can be made available to opam by running the following commands.
```bash
opam repo add coq-released "https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released"
opam repo add iris-dev "https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/opam.git"
opam update
opam pin add -n -y cerberus-lib "git+https://github.com/rems-project/cerberus.git#f11e6b335a687c1b77539f7e5695607d09dfc3ea"
```
You can then finally install RefinedC with the following command, or rather
decide to install it from a local clone to have access to various examples.
```bash
opam pin add refinedc "git+https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/refinedc.git"
```

To install RefinedC from a local clone you can run the following commands.
```bash
git clone "https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/refinedc.git"
opam pin add refinedc refinedc
```
You can then start checking annotated C files in the repository using, for
example, the following command.
```bash
cd refinedc
refinedc check examples/queue.c
```

## Verifying a program from scratch using RefinedC

In this section we will see how one can create a new RefinedC project and
verify a first (trivial) program example. It is assumed that RefinedC has
been installed following the above instructions.

### Source project setup

In the following, we will assume that the user's code lives in a directory
`c_example` with the following structure.
```
├── Makefile
└── src
    └── example.c
```
File `Makefile`:
```make
all: src/example
.PHONY: all

src/example: src/example.c
	gcc -Wno-attributes -o $@ $<

clean:
	rm -f src/example
.PHONY: clean
```
File `src/example.c`:
```c
#include <assert.h>

unsigned int add3(unsigned int x, unsigned int y, unsigned int z){
  unsigned int r = x + y;
  return r + z;
}

int main(){
  unsigned int a;

  a = add3(1, 2, 3);
  assert(a == 6u);

  a = add3(a, a, a);
  assert(a == 18u);

  return 0;
}
```
Of course, bigger projects, with more source files and more complex directory
structure will work just as well, but we start simple so that you can see how
things work more easily.

### RefinedC project creation

The first step for verifying a C program using RefinedC is to set up a new
RefinedC project. To do so, you must run the following command at the root of
the source tree (i.e., exactly where you would typically run `git init`).
```bash
cd c_example
refinedc init
```
If all goes well, `refinedc init` will report that a RefinedC project has been
initialized in your `c_example` directory, and it should also give the logical
Coq directory (i.e., the module path) that will be used as a prefix for every
Coq module of your project. Its default value is based on the name of the
project directory, but this behaviour can be overridden. (Note that you can
use `refinedc init --help` to see what options are available.)

After having successfully initialised the RefinedC project, your `c_example`
directory should contain the following.
```
├── _CoqProject       ← Coq project file, maintained by RefinedC.
├── dune-project      ← Dune project file, used by RefinedC internally.
├── Makefile
├── rc-project.toml   ← RefinedC project configuration
└── src
    └── example.c
```
The generated files should not be edited directly, to the exception of the
project configuration file `rc-project.toml`, which is used to configure
certain things like C preprocessor options or Coq dependencies. For now, you
don't need to worry about it.

### Running RefinedC

We are now ready to actually run RefinedC on our C source file. So, go ahead
and run the following command.
```bash
refinedc check src/example.c
```
If everything goes well, this command will generate the necessary Coq files,
and then automatically run Coq to check them. Let us have a look to the files
contained in our project folder to see what happened.
```
├── _build                             ← Dune build directory.
├── _CoqProject
├── dune-project
├── Makefile
├── rc-project.toml
└── src
    ├── example.c
    └── proofs                         ← Coq files for all C files in [src].
        └── example                    ← Coq files for [src/example.c].
            ├── dune                   ← Generated dune file.
            ├── generated_code.v       ← Generated code file.
            ├── generated_proof_add3.v ← Generated proof file for [add3].
            ├── generated_proof_main.v ← Generated proof file for [main].
            ├── generated_spec.v       ← Generated specification file.
            └── proof_files            ← Internally used file.
```
You can see that a whole bunch of files have been generated inside a new
directory `src/proofs/example`. This directory gathers all Coq files that
are specific to the `src/example.c` file. It contains generated files, but
the user can also write their own Coq source files there. Note that we use
the convention that generated Coq files are prefixed with `generated_`. Note
also that Coq compilation does not directly happen in the source directory,
but in the `_build` directory, which is automatically created by calling the
`dune` build system (used by RefinedC internally).

You might now wonder: what have we proved about our program? And the answer
is: nothing. Indeed, RefinedC checks function specifications, but such specs
must be provided by the user. So far we have not given any RefinedC spec for
our two functions `add3` and `main`. In fact, if you edit the proof file at
`src/proofs/example/generated_proof_add3.v` you will see that it only holds
a comment saying that the function has no spec. And similarly, if you look at
the file `src/proofs/example/generated_spec.v` you will see that none of our
functions have a specification (they have been skipped).

### A spec for `add3`

Let us now do some actual RefinedC verification and give a specification to
our `add3` function. Specifications are given as attributes attached to the
function definitions (or prototypes). The valid attributes and the RefinedC
syntax are documented in [ANNOTATIONS.md](ANNOTATIONS.md), you can consult it
later if you want to learn more. For now, we will introduce what we need en
passant.

In RefinedC, a function specification is given by a type. And as one might
expect, the type of a function is specified by giving a type for each of the
arguments and a type for the return value. The C type of the arguments and
the return type of `add3` are all `unsigned int`. The corresponding RefinedC
type is `int<u32>`, so you can edit `src/example.c` as follows.
```c
[[rc::args("int<u32>", "int<u32>", "int<u32>")]]
[[rc::returns("int<u32>")]]
unsigned int add3(unsigned int x, unsigned int y, unsigned int z){
  unsigned int r = x + y;
  return r + z;
}
```
Here, the `rc::args` annotation gives the type for each function argument (in
order), and the `rc::returns` annotation gives the type of the return value.

Let us now see what happens if we run RefinedC again.
```bash
refinedc check src/example.c
```
This time the system actually attempts to prove something, but it fails with
two error messages of the following form (abbreviated).
```
Cannot solve sidecondition in function "add3" !
```
Next to the messages, Coq goals are shown to tell us what it is that could not
be proved. In our case, both goals are of the form `_ + _ ≤ max_int u32`. That
explains the error: the additions in our `add3` function can overflow (which
leads to undefined behaviour in RefinedC).

To solve this problem we need to extend the function specification using two
pre-conditions. However, these preconditions need to mention the actual value
of the function arguments, which is not yet available in the specification. To
this aim we must use refinement types of the form `n @ int<u32>`, Intuitively
corresponding to a singleton (integer) type with value `n`.
```
[[rc::parameters("nx : nat", "ny : nat", "nz : nat")]]
[[rc::args("nx @ int<u32>", "ny @ int<u32>", "nz @ int<u32>")]]
[[rc::requires("{nx + ny ≤ max_int u32}", "{(nx + ny) + nz ≤ max_int u32}")]]
[[rc::returns("int<u32>")]]
unsigned int add3(unsigned int x, unsigned int y, unsigned int z){
  unsigned int r = x + y;
  return r + z;
}
```
Note that the `rc::parameters` annotation is used to introduced universally
quantified variables in the specifications. Here all such variables are given
the Coq type `nat`, and the pre-conditions given with `rc::requires` are
expressed as Coq propositions (wrapped in braces to escape to Coq syntax).
After this modification, the specification is successfully checked by calling
RefinedC.
```bash
refinedc check src/example.c
```

### Verifying `main`

Let us now turn to the `main` function, whose specification should be fairly
trivial: it take no arguments and returns an integer which happens to always
be `0`. This can be expressed using the following RefinedC spec.
```c
[[rc::returns("{0} @ int<i32>")]]
int main(){
  unsigned int a;

  a = add3(1, 2, 3);
  assert(a == 6u);

  a = add3(a, a, a);
  assert(a == 18u);

  return 0;
}
```
One important thing that this spec implies is that the evaluation of `main`
does not fail. In particular, RefinedC needs to check that the assertions will
never fail. Let us check if it is able to do so.
```bash
refinedc check src/example.c
```

Not quite! And the reason is that the specification of `add3` is too weak: it
only says that its return value is an unsigned integer. In particular, its
return value is not linked to its arguments in any way. Hence, it is not very
surprising that RefinedC cannot establish that the result of `add3(1, 2, 3)`
is equal to `6u`.

To fix this, we can change the return type of `add3` to be the following.
```c
[[rc::returns("{nx + ny + nz} @ int<u32>")]]
```
With this modification, the verification finally goes through.
```bash
refinedc check src/example.c
```
Congratulations, you have verified your first C program using RefinedC!

What you write, what the tool generates
The verifier checks the proof; it does not necessarily write it.
“Authored” below means supplied by the verification author (in this experiment, the assistant). “Generated” means emitted by the verification tool. Automatic tactic execution is distinct from automatic proof-script generation.
ToolYou write / maintainTool generates / executesHow C enters the proof
VSTC; Rocq funspecs; loop assertions; helper lemmas; Floyd tactic scripts for every program.clightgen generates the Clight AST. Rocq executes your Floyd script and checks the proof. It does not generate verif_pN.v.External clightgen → generated .v → coqc → Require Import CPrograms.…
RefinedCC; rc:: contracts, types and loop annotations. P3 adds a helper lemma and tactics; P4 adds tactics.C representation, Rocq specification and proof script. Lithium automates the generated proof, using supplied hooks; Rocq checks it.refinedc check reads annotated C and builds generated_code/spec/proof files.
WPC; ACSL predicates, contracts, loop invariants, variants and assertions. No separate proof script in this experiment.RTE and functional VCs; Qed/Why3/Alt-Ergo attempt to close them. P5 remains open.frama-c reads the annotated C directly.
AutoCorres2C; theory import/setup; HOL contracts, invariants, measures, helper lemmas and proof methods.install_C_file generates the C model; autocorres generates an abstraction and correspondence proofs. Isabelle checks your correctness proof.install_C_file and autocorres commands inside the authored theory.
“Fully automatic” in the metrics means no manual proof steps after supplying the specification. It does not mean that contracts or loop invariants were inferred.
Notable projects and applications
Published applications, separate from our five-program experiment. A verified component does not imply that its entire parent project is verified.
ToolRecognizable project / applicationWhat the evidence establishes
VSTOpenSSL HMAC / SHA-256Research verification of cryptographic C components, including functional correctness and a cryptographic security connection—not a verification of all OpenSSL. Verified correctness and security of OpenSSL HMAC; VST applications bibliography.
RefinedCRefinedProsa / Rössl schedulerResearch application connecting RefinedC’s C proofs with Prosa’s response-time analysis for the Rössl interrupt-free scheduler. This is a named research case study, not evidence of widespread production deployment. RefinedProsa project and paper.
Frama-C/WPContiki linked-list module; Mitsubishi Electric R&D experimentsContiki component verification with WP; published industrial experiments at Mitsubishi Electric R&D Centre Europe use Frama-C plug-ins including WP, Eva and PathCrawler. This does not mean that all Contiki or all industrial analyses use WP. Ghosts for Lists: a critical module of Contiki; Frama-C publications: ten years of Mitsubishi experiments.
Isabelle/HOL + AutoCorres2seL4 (Isabelle/HOL ecosystem)seL4’s kernel proofs use Isabelle/HOL. Original AutoCorres lives in the seL4/l4v tool suite; AutoCorres2 is a separate AFP fork. The seL4 result should not be attributed wholesale to AutoCorres2. seL4 proof scope; AutoCorres in l4v; AutoCorres2 provenance.

Require Import VST.floyd.proofauto.
Require Import CPrograms.p3_sum.
#[export] Instance CompSpecs : compspecs. make_compspecs prog. Defined.
Definition Vprog : varspecs. mk_varspecs prog. Defined.
Definition sumZ : list Z -> Z := fold_right Z.add 0.
Lemma sumZ_app : forall a b, sumZ (a++b) = sumZ a + sumZ b.
Proof. intros. induction a; simpl; lia. Qed.
Lemma prefix_step : forall xs i,
  0 <= i < Zlength xs ->
  sumZ (sublist 0 (i+1) xs) = sumZ (sublist 0 i xs) + Znth i xs.
Proof.
  intros. rewrite (sublist_split 0 i (i+1)) by lia.
  rewrite sumZ_app, (sublist_one i) by lia. simpl. lia.
Qed.

 WITH a : val, xs : list Z, n : Z

     forall k, 0 <= k <= n ->

¹ Human-written separate proof lines, including scaffolding and helper lemmas; generated RefinedC proofs are listed separately. ² Static tactic occurrences for Rocq, method invocations for Isabelle; not execution counts or directly equivalent units of effort.
Nonblank physical lines. Specs include predicates, contracts and external loop assertions; annotations are in-C attributes/comments. Proof lines include separate scaffolding and helper lemmas. See line_audit for every counted line. Manual steps are syntactic tactic occurrences (Rocq) or apply/by/proof(method) invocations (Isabelle); control combinators are not expanded. Embedded RefinedC tactics count as manual. Generated proofs are separately reported. What must be trusted?
Every column also relies on the adequacy of its specification and C semantics, plus the implementation/runtime of its trusted checker and the hardware.

The source front-end and semantic correspondence are boundaries. Printed theorem dependencies include classical logic, functional/propositional extensionality, ensemble extensionality and classical Dedekind-real decisions. No SMT oracle. CompCert offers a compiler connection, but this study does not instantiate it.

↓

The C translation and formal C model remain boundaries. The generated theorem audit reports closed under the global context for all six function/case proofs. Custom P3/P4 lemmas and tactics are checked by Rocq. No compiler link.

Trust the front-end, memory model, VC generator, simplifier, Why3 driver and SMT solver. These runs do not replay SMT certificates in a proof-assistant kernel. The JSON success harness is also part of the experiment’s reporting boundary.

AutoCorres2

↓

The C parser and interpretation of its formal semantics remain boundaries. Abstraction correspondence proofs are generated. Project theories disable quick_and_dirty and fail if their correctness theorems depend on any oracle. Isabelle/HOL’s logical axioms remain trusted. No verified compiler chain was instantiated.

RLVR: P3 and P4 as reward oracles
ToolInvariant emitted by LLMNo human proof script?Measured latencyFailure / determinismAssessment
WPSource ACSLYes for these two programs; annotations suffice.P3: 1.682 s / P4: 3.196 sJSON per goal; all three outcomes agree. Timeout ≠ counterexample.Best first pilot for fast source-level invariant rewards.
RefinedCSource rc::inv_vars / constraintsNot from invariants alone here: fixed P3 helper lemma and P3/P4 tactic hooks were needed.P3: 4.237 s / P4: 9.058 sNonzero exit + detailed text; all three outcomes agree.Strong Rocq-kernel option if the helper proof scaffold is fixed.

Ratings are task-based judgments, not broad capability or determinism claims. The timings are cold local checks with prebuilt libraries, not an optimized persistent-server oracle.
Freeze C, contracts, helper lemmas and checker commands. Permit only invariant edits. Reward only a nonempty expected obligation set with every safety/functional goal closed; reject skipped proofs and stale artifacts. Keep invalid, timed-out and infrastructure-error outcomes distinct.
Verdict for a researcher with a Rocq background
Pilot RefinedC for annotation-driven Rocq proofs.
Use WP first for a practical invariant-generation oracle.
On this set, RefinedC checks all five programs, including reversal without manual tactics. P3/P4 still need pure reasoning hooks, so it is not an invariant-only oracle out of the box. The exact Rocq/Iris/Lithium pins are a maintenance cost.
Choose VST when explicit separation-logic proofs, flexible assertions and the potential CompCert connection matter more than annotation brevity. Its symbolic execution is approachable from Rocq, but signed arithmetic and heap entailments required more explicit work here.
AutoCorres2 checks the whole set with total-correctness proofs. Its exception-aware loop rule, typed heaps and word/integer conversions added learning work in this experiment. Move it to the front for Isabelle/seL4 integration.
WP was the fastest measured pipeline on the successful scalar/array cases and gave structured VC feedback. The inductive heap proof is unfinished; that is a limit of this proof attempt, not evidence that WP cannot verify reversal.
What would change the answer?
Larger code, concurrency, unions/casts, existing proof libraries, stronger framing, persistent-oracle latency, or a requirement to connect to compiled code. A fair follow-up would align memory preconditions and termination guarantees, then compare maintenance after code changes.
All scope limitations
  • Function-level correctness under displayed preconditions; no whole-program linking, executable compiler theorem, or end-to-end binary verification was instantiated.
  • VST semax_body and RefinedC typed_function establish safety and functional partial correctness. Separate termination proofs were not supplied for these tools. AutoCorres2 runs_to proves total correctness; WP includes termination obligations.
  • VST and RefinedC array contracts own initialized arrays; WP permits read-only initialized arrays. These are different admissible memory states, including potentially different empty-array pointer domains.
  • P5 VST and RefinedC specify reversal of the value sequence. AutoCorres2 and the unfinished WP contract additionally preserve node identities and values. Frame specifications are not identical across tools.
  • AutoCorres2 P1/P3 omit limits.h, used only by ACSL in the shared source. RefinedC adds attributes, refinedc.h and a typedef for node pointers. Executable function bodies are unchanged apart from whitespace.
  • This is a small cold-local-build case study with prebuilt libraries and warm OS caches, not a controlled general performance ranking. RSS is a per-process high-water mark, not aggregate memory.
  • WP P5 stays open. No interactive Rocq discharge or certificate is claimed; no VST-A experiment was performed.
Reproduce and host on your LAN
The repo provides scripts/install.sh, one run.sh per tool, results/measure.py and presentation/build.sh. Run bash presentation/serve.sh, then open http://HOST-LAN-IP:8000 on another device. The serving container mounts only this presentation directory.
Full reproduction instructions
# Deductive C verification experiment

## Publish with Cloudflare Pages

The GitHub repository is `ExcitedSpider/itp-c-lab`. Pages serves the committed
`public/index.html`; no prover installation or build runs on Cloudflare.

After changing the lab, rebuild and package using the existing container:

```sh
podman exec c-itp-wp python3 presentation/build.py
podman exec c-itp-wp python3 presentation/package_site.py
bash scripts/publish-github.sh
```

The push script selects the existing `ExcitedAgent` login for this process and
verifies the account before pushing via HTTPS. It does not switch the global
GitHub profile or use the default SSH identity.

In Cloudflare **Workers & Pages**, create a **Pages** project connected to
`ExcitedSpider/itp-c-lab`: production branch `main`, framework preset **None**,
build command blank, build output directory `public`, root directory default.
Under the project's **Custom domains**, add `itp-c.qiuyif.org` and complete the
Cloudflare DNS setup. Subsequent pushes to `main` deploy the committed output.

## Explore the lab

Open `presentation/index.html` directly: a self-contained offline verification
lab with independent program and prover lists. Choose one of the 20 cases to
inspect its real sources, proofs, metrics and checker outputs. Setup, comparison
charts, notable projects, TCB and RLVR notes are expandable reference sections.
There is no slide navigation; Previous/Next controls only step through proofs.
VST and RefinedC tabs include offline proof steppers: actual Rocq responses and
`Show.` goal inspections recorded command by command, with source highlighting.
These are navigable recordings, not a live jsCoq checker; editing or checking
new tactics is not supported. RefinedC generated proofs and the authored P3
helper proof are labeled separately. AutoCorres2 also has recorded Isabelle
states for all five programs, using the same controls and arrow keys. WP shows
VC reports rather than an interactive proof script.
The authoritative experiment is in `results/rework/`. Earlier records in
`results/logs/` and JavaScript runners are historical and superseded.
The earlier installation-blocked diagnosis was incorrect. Direct Podman commands
worked without changing permissions. All four toolchains are installed.

| Tool | P1 abs | P2 swap + alias | P3 sum | P4 search | P5 reverse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VST-Floyd | checked | checked | checked | checked | checked |
| RefinedC | checked | checked | checked | checked | checked |
| Frama-C/WP | checked | checked | checked | checked | **partial** |
| AutoCorres2 | checked | checked | checked | checked | checked |

These are function-level safety and correctness proofs under the displayed
contracts. VST and RefinedC establish partial correctness; separate termination
proofs were not supplied. AutoCorres2 proves total correctness. WP includes
termination VCs. No compiler/linking theorem was instantiated. No admitted
project proof is counted as success. WP P5 closes 7/15 console obligations;
eight remain open after timeout. No interactive Rocq discharge is claimed.

## Reproduce in Podman

From this directory, with Podman available:

```sh
bash scripts/install.sh
bash vst/run.sh
bash refinedc/run.sh
bash wp/run.sh
bash autocorres/run.sh
podman exec c-itp-wp python3 results/measure.py
bash presentation/build.sh
```

Proof-state recordings are embedded in the HTML and stored under
`results/rework/proof-states/`, with exact commands, raw responses and source
hashes. After changing proof sources, regenerate them with
`bash presentation/record-proofs.sh` before building the page. This requires
the generated Clight and RefinedC dependencies already built; after a full
RefinedC check (which cleans between cases), restore all positive dependencies
with `podman exec c-itp-refinedc python3 refinedc/audit.py`. The builder rejects
stale recordings whose source hashes no longer match. Each compound tactic
is a single recorded step; the replay does not expand its internal execution.

For Isabelle alone: `podman exec c-itp-autocorres python3 autocorres/record.py`.
The capture sessions in `autocorres/recording/` load the unchanged original
theories with `Thy_Info.use_theories` and `record_theories=true`, then export
`Toplevel.pretty_state` after each parsed command. This includes actual Isar
goals and focused subgoals, not reconstructed build-log summaries. Theories
load under the capture namespace `Draft`; their source and proofs are unchanged.
Session commands/output and raw XML are in `results/rework/autocorres-record-p*.txt`
and `autocorres-p*-states.xml`. Empty state output means no open proof state;
other command messages remain in the session log. Each original theory's oracle
audit also executes, and skipped proofs are rejected by the recorder.

Each checker runs every positive case three times and checks a deliberately
broken P3 invariant. WP exits 2 while P5 remains partial; continue with the other
commands. The install script reproduces recorded operations and reuses project
containers; the script itself has not had a clean-room end-to-end test. Actual
installations and checks are logged. No host packages were installed. Separate
container-local switches isolate the Rocq/OCaml stacks.

Exact versions, image digests and logs are in `results/rework/setup.json`:

- VST 2.17, Rocq 9.1.0, stdlib 9.0.0, CompCert opam package 3.18.
  Installed `clightgen` reports 3.17; both strings are retained.
- RefinedC/Lithium commit `2e89846baeaa7f65cbe17e3ae7297a8ed5b4feca`,
  Rocq 9.1.0, Iris `dev.2026-09-10.3.b3495ef9`, stdpp
  `dev.2026-09-09.1.c3186aad`. Compatibility was checked before installation.
  The executable reports `2e89846-dirty` despite a clean source checkout.
- Frama-C 32.0 Germanium, Why3 1.8.2, Alt-Ergo 2.5.4, OCaml 4.14.2.
  Ordinary WP/Why3 invocation works; no exported-VC fallback is used.
- Isabelle2025-2, AFP 2026-10-16, Poly/ML 5.9.2. The image needed cpp;
  the missing-preprocessor error and successful retry are retained.

Recorded VST installation took about 17 minutes and RefinedC about 10 minutes.
AutoCorres2's parent build failed after about 6 minutes; after installing cpp,
the retry took about 8 minutes. These are observations, not clean-machine setup
benchmarks. Exact commands, exit codes, times and outputs are in `results/rework/`.

## Host on your LAN

```sh
bash presentation/serve.sh
```

Open `http://HOST-LAN-IP:8000` on another device on the same network, or
`http://localhost:8000` on this machine. Use the host address, not a container IP.
If the host firewall blocks TCP 8000, allow it on your trusted LAN. Ctrl-C stops
the disposable serving container. Only the presentation directory is served.
Use `LAB_PORT=8080 bash presentation/serve.sh` to select another port.

## Contracts and C differences

- P1 excludes INT_MIN and proves mathematical absolute value.
- P2 permits identical or separate pointers. VST and RefinedC prove separate
  specs for the two cases; WP and AutoCorres2 admit aliasing in one contract.
- P3 bounds every prefix sum by signed-int limits, including intermediate sums.
- P4 supports duplicates and empty arrays; proves a matching index or absence;
  uses a half-open interval and `lo+(hi-lo)/2` to avoid overflow.
- P5 uses finite inductive/recursive lists. VST and RefinedC prove reversed
  values; AutoCorres2 and unfinished WP also preserve node identities and values.
  Frame and ownership contracts are not identical.

VST and RefinedC own initialized arrays; WP permits read-only initialized
storage. Empty-array pointer domains can differ. AutoCorres2's default ARM model
uses 32-bit pointers; the other tested environments use x86_64/i32. RefinedC adds
attributes, a header and a node typedef. AutoCorres2 P1/P3 omit limits.h, used
only in ACSL. Executable function bodies otherwise match. The AutoCorres2 P5
proof adapts AFP ListRev and retains its BSD attribution. No VST-A run was made.

## Metrics and oracle boundaries

`results/rework/metrics.json` enumerates every counted physical line and every
recognized manual tactic/method occurrence. These are syntactic counts, not
executed tactics or equivalent units of cognitive effort. Generated RefinedC
proof text is separate; human proof scaffolding is included. External loop
assertions count as specifications.

Times are medians of three fresh local checks, including front-end and startup,
with installed libraries/AFP parent heaps retained. Tools ran sequentially.
RefinedC P2 sums alias and separate-case checks. RSS is the largest process
high-water mark, not total concurrent memory. Repeated Boolean outcomes agree;
this is not a general determinism guarantee. WP P5 times a failed attempt.
Recorded source hashes bind proof measurements to their inputs.

All four reject the +1 accumulator invariant. WP exposes JSON VC outcomes;
other runners retain process/session status and textual goals. An RL reward
must freeze C, contracts and helpers; reject stale/skipped proofs; require all
expected obligations; distinguish timeout, invalidity and infrastructure errors.
WP was fastest for these successful array cases. RefinedC is a useful Rocq-backed
pilot but P3/P4 need fixed pure-proof hooks. VST needs Floyd scaffolding;
AutoCorres2 needs HOL proofs and measures. Isabelle becomes more compelling
when integrating with seL4.

The presentation details the TCB and observed learning costs. VST's assumptions
include classical/extensionality axioms. RefinedC's six generated function/case
theorems audit closed under the global context. AutoCorres2 disables
quick_and_dirty and rejects oracle dependencies. WP trusts the VC pipeline
and SMT results without kernel certificate replay.
